punchline: A rich minister pitied a monk who lived on rice and beans, and the monk's one-line answer handed the pity right back.
thirty_sec: In J. L. Collins's book, a minister to the king looks at his old friend, a thin monk in shabby clothes, and feels sorry for him. Learn to cater to the king, he says, and you could eat better. The monk turns it around: learn to live on rice and beans and you would not have to cater to anyone. Collins uses the story to say wealth means freedom, and his example is the ability to say no.
